er_v06_c06_b101_01: The sack pokes through the door first, its corners worn fuzzy.
er_v06_c06_b101_03: I picked some things up. Asked around at the dump—they said this stuff sells.
er_v06_c06_b101_04: Do you buy it or not?
er_v06_c06_b101_05: She sets the sack on the counter. The mouth slackens, and a few old casings and a bundle of wire slide out.
er_v06_c06_b101_07: Easy. There are some connectors in there. I don't want them snapped.
er_v06_c06_b101_08: This casing is dented, but the inside's fine.
er_v06_c06_b101_09: This one looks new, but the connector's rusted. That comes off the price.
er_v06_c06_b101_11: I didn't pick it with my eyes shut.
er_v06_c06_b101_12: The pile underneath is the stuff I left. It was scattered on the ground, wet.
er_v06_c06_b101_13: Don't bring the wet batch. Rust kills the value.
er_v06_c06_b101_14: I know. That's why I only brought the dry ones.
er_v06_c06_b101_15: The shopkeeper splits the casings into two piles and pulls out a blackened length of wire.
er_v06_c06_b106_02: She presses the credits into her palm and moves them one by one into the inner pocket of her shawl.
er_v06_c06_b106_05: To hire someone to look into something.
er_v06_c06_b106_06: There are people down here. They read files, they can get into records rooms.
er_v06_c06_b106_09: Security won't admit they're wrong. They're holding my mother, and the charge still stands.
er_v06_c06_b106_10: The case stays open, she stays inside.
er_v06_c06_b106_11: I need someone on the outside to go through that file.
er_v06_c06_b106_13: I know. That's why tomorrow I'm cleaning grow tanks.
er_v06_c06_b106_14: One day, two meals, and they pay.
er_v06_c06_b106_15: The work's filthy. The tank walls are covered in green. Three washes and my hands still won't feel clean.
er_v06_c06_b106_17: Don't soak your hands too long.
er_v06_c06_b106_19: If you've got odd jobs, tell me too.
er_v06_c06_b106_20: I'll call you if there's work.
er_v06_c06_b106_21: Pay the going rate. Don't tell me later that you helped me, so it should be less.
er_v06_c06_b106_24: Someone where I'm staying ran out of soap and didn't say a word. I'll bring two bars back next time.
er_v06_c06_b106_25: You still have that soap? The cheap kind.
er_v06_c06_b106_27: Put it on credit. I'll pay tomorrow.
er_v06_c06_b106_29: Stop giving me nutrifruit. I've eaten it for half a month. Now the sight of the skin turns my stomach.
er_v06_c06_b106_32: She folds the sack twice, tucks it under her arm, and stops only at the door.
er_v06_c06_b106_33: Hey. I'll be back late tomorrow.
er_v06_c06_b106_34: If you've got something before closing, keep my goods aside.

er_v06_c07_b101_01: This time she carries two bags—one stuffed full, one only half.
er_v06_c07_b101_02: Today's different. I sorted it myself first.
er_v06_c07_b101_03: One pile for usable, one for not. Don't mix them.
er_v06_c07_b101_04: She sets the bags apart and pushes both mouths toward the shopkeeper.
er_v06_c07_b101_05: I counted this pile three times.
er_v06_c07_b101_06: Long wire in one bundle, short in another. I'm not mixing them to cheat you.
er_v06_c07_b101_08: Borrowed the ration station's scale. Left a cup as deposit.
er_v06_c07_b101_09: The cup you sold me last time has a chip on the bottom. It leaks.
er_v06_c07_b101_11: Don't bother. I use it with a cloth under it.
er_v06_c07_b101_12: I'll name the price first. Listen.
er_v06_c07_b101_13: I worked this lot out. It's worth this.
er_v06_c07_b101_14: She names the number, taps a nail twice on the counter, and waits.
er_v06_c07_b106_02: There are buyers at the docks.
er_v06_c07_b106_04: They squeeze hard. Their scale's off too.
er_v06_c07_b106_06: Look, but don't leave all your goods with them.
er_v06_c07_b106_08: I'm not going there to beg.
er_v06_c07_b106_09: Still a way from eight hundred. A long way.
er_v06_c07_b106_10: The foreman at the grow tanks says there's more pay when the next batch is cleaned. No idea when.
er_v06_c07_b106_11: He said I don't look like I've done rough work.
er_v06_c07_b106_14: He laughed. I don't see what's funny.
er_v06_c07_b106_15: Soak in those tanks long enough and your hands wrinkle. The wrinkles don't wash out.
er_v06_c07_b106_17: She turns her palm up, lays it on the counter for two seconds, then pulls it back.
er_v06_c07_b106_18: Dry them after. Not with hot water.
er_v06_c07_b106_19: You have to put a word in everything.
er_v06_c07_b106_20: Fine. I'll bring a cloth next time.
er_v06_c08_b101_01: A day later she comes in holding one thing, wrapped in cloth.
er_v06_c08_b101_02: No stock today. Just this one piece.
er_v06_c08_b101_03: The cloth comes away. Inside is an offcut, all its connectors intact, the surface unmarked.
er_v06_c08_b101_04: Don't price this with the rest. It's for you.
er_v06_c08_b101_06: No use to me. I've got nothing that connects to it.
er_v06_c08_b101_07: A waste to throw away. At least someone here knows what it is.
er_v06_c08_b101_09: I said it doesn't count as money.
er_v06_c08_b101_10: Paying a fair price for what I scavenge counts as helping. I've said that.
er_v06_c08_b101_11: I don't pretend help didn't happen.
er_v06_c08_b102_01: I'll take it. Off the books.
er_v06_c08_b102_03: She folds the cloth and tucks it back into her shawl—slower than she talks.
er_v06_c08_b102_04: Don't think this makes you owe me.
er_v06_c08_b102_05: I pay back what I take. If you accept it, I can keep coming.
er_v06_c08_b103_01: This is something I wanted to give you. If you insist on paying, fine.
er_v06_c08_b103_02: But know this: this time I'm not the one asking.
er_v06_c08_b104_01: You won't take it? Fine. Next time I'll pick something you can't find a reason to refuse.
er_v06_c08_b105_01: You really don't stand on ceremony.
er_v06_c08_b105_02: I picked through two lots to find this one. The first had a crooked connector. I threw it out.
er_v06_c08_b105_03: Don't think I grabbed it at random.
er_v06_c08_b105_05: If you can tell, don't say it.
er_v06_c08_b105_06: If you say it, it'll be awkward to bring a second one.
er_v06_c08_b105_07: She walks to the shelf and straightens one bar of soap.
er_v06_c08_b105_11: Just this row. The rest is your problem.
er_v06_c08_b106_01: She walks to the shelf and straightens one bar of soap.
er_v06_c08_b106_05: Just this row. The rest is your problem.
er_v06_c09_b101_01: The shop is quiet that afternoon when a woman in a bright shawl pushes the door open.
er_v06_c09_b101_03: I thought I had the wrong place. This hinge really needs oil.
er_v06_c09_b102_01: I'm Lydia. An old friend of Eleanor's. Very old.
er_v06_c09_b102_02: She's not here, is she? I picked a time she'd be out.
er_v06_c09_b102_04: Lydia sets a glittering bracelet on the counter.
er_v06_c09_b102_05: This. Can you tell good goods?
er_v06_c09_b102_06: I'll name a number first. Don't laugh if it's too low.
er_v06_c09_b102_08: She names an absurdly low price, eyes fixed on the shopkeeper.
er_v06_c09_b106_01: Eleanor's been selling things here lately?
er_v06_c09_b106_03: She never used to touch any of this.
er_v06_c09_b106_04: I found her a job upstairs.
er_v06_c09_b106_07: Don't bring up her mother's case in public.
er_v06_c09_b106_09: I didn't think it was a big deal.
er_v06_c09_b106_10: She heard it and her whole face changed.
er_v06_c09_b106_14: I really thought the job could help her.
er_v06_c09_b106_15: ...No. Wait. If she asks, tell her I came to sell something.
er_v06_c09_b106_16: Just don't make me sound better than I was.
er_v06_c09_b107_01: She gathers her shawl and glances at the bracelet once more before leaving.
er_v06_c10_b101_01: The next day Eleanor pushes the door open with no sack in her hands.
er_v06_c10_b102_02: A bracelet. She really let it go.
er_v06_c10_b102_03: Did she also mention a job?
er_v06_c10_b103_01: The box? I remember that business.
er_v06_c10_b103_02: Did she also mention a job?
er_v06_c10_b104_02: Did she also mention a job?
er_v06_c10_b105_01: She said they need people upstairs. Good money.
er_v06_c10_b105_02: The condition is I can't mention my mother's case in public.
er_v06_c10_b105_08: If I took that job, I'd have to keep quiet.
er_v06_c10_b105_09: My mother's still in there. I can't keep quiet.
er_v06_c10_b105_10: I haven't saved eight hundred. Haven't found a detective either.
er_v06_c10_b105_11: But I won't bury her case for a job.
er_v06_c10_b105_13: I thought you'd tell me to take it.
er_v06_c10_b105_15: That's easy for you to say.
er_v06_c10_b105_16: She rests her hand on the counter and stays like that for a moment.
er_v06_c10_b106_01: No goods today. I just came to tell you.
er_v06_c10_b106_03: She reaches the door and stops.
er_v06_c06_b003_01: Good. You take the goods, I take the credits.
er_v06_c06_b003_02: This is much better than standing here waiting for you to pity me.
er_v06_c06_b004_01: You paid too much. This lot will sell well, right?
er_v06_c06_b004_02: Then you'll have to tell me what it's normally worth. I have to learn.
er_v06_c06_b005_01: Is that price because the goods aren't worth much, or because you think I can only sell to you?
er_v06_c06_b006_01: It's fine. I'll remember what you don't buy and bring something else next time.
er_v06_c07_b006_01: Now I know that buying what I scavenged at a fair price counts as help too.
er_v06_c07_b007_01: Don't tell me again that this is just what the lower levels pay. I've asked other buyers.
er_v06_c07_b007_02: It's worth what it's worth. My being desperate doesn't make it cheaper.
er_v06_c09_b002_01: This quality, and you'll pay that? You even noticed the clasp was replaced?
er_v06_c09_b003_02: She said you never take advantage of people. I suppose it depends on whose advantage it is.
er_v06_c09_b004_01: You won't buy it? Fine. At least you didn't pretend to know.
